app.notes:
### Added

- **1000 Hz polling, disconnect when docked, and one-frame audio reports** (firmware protocol 1.22, upstream's batch adapted). Your board's page: Connection to the PC's polling rate gets 1000 Hz (the controller's latest state every millisecond) beside 250 Hz, 500 Hz and Real-time (each Bluetooth report as it arrives; it was labelled "1 kHz"); Power gets **Disconnect when docked** (off by default: the controller's Bluetooth turns off when you put it on a charging station or dock); and the Controller page's Haptic feedback section gets **Audio reports**, Two frames (the default) or One frame, to compare haptic feedback and delay. All three are saved by the save bar like any board setting, and the simulated board speaks 1.22.
- **The Pico 2 W page shows what the board reports about itself** (firmware protocol 1.21). With firmware that has its new identity report, the board zone's spec line names the chip's package (RP2350A) and the flash size the board measured at start-up (its ⓘ says what the firmware is built for), the board's facts say what it presents itself to the PC as (DualSense), and a display other than the Waveshare Pico-OLED-1.3, or a display change waiting for the next start, is shown. When the board has less flash than its firmware expects, the zone says settings can't be saved on it. Update offers use this report instead of the board's name, so a board that measured a smaller flash isn't offered an image that needs more. Older firmware works as before.
- **Linux: Remove USB access setup.** Set up USB access now has its undo on your board's page (Connection to the PC): it lists the files it deletes (the USB rule and, where the app installed it, the sandbox profile), shows the exact script, and runs it only when you press Remove (your password, as for the setup). Set up USB access puts them back. In all 7 languages.
- **Games: remove a DualSense Proton build.** The DualSense Proton build section lists each of our builds on this PC with its folders, and offers Remove for one that no game and no launcher default uses (it asks first; a build still in use says what uses it). While Steam or Heroic is running, Remove leaves the build in place and says which to close first. Each update used to leave the older build behind for good. In all 7 languages.

### Removed

- **The switched-off welcome tour is gone from the app.** It had been turned off since the layout changed and never showed, but its screens, texts, voice lines and styles still shipped. The narrator's hint in App settings no longer mentions it. A new tour is planned (About → Coming soon).

### Fixed

- **Ctrl+R no longer reloads the app (and can't cut a firmware update short).** Electron's built-in menu was still active behind the hidden menu bar: Ctrl+R / ⌘R or F5 reloaded the page, which during a firmware update stopped the write halfway and dropped unsaved button, stick and calibration changes; Ctrl+Shift+I opened the developer tools in releases; Ctrl+= zoomed past the fixed 100 %. The app now has its own menu (none on Windows and Linux; App, Edit and Window on macOS) and refuses those keys.
- **Linux: the app no longer deletes other programs' downloads or your own copy.** At every start it removed any `*.AppImage.part` file in its folder (often Downloads), including a browser's download still in progress, and a real file you kept under the name `DS5Dongle-OLED-Edition-Configurator.AppImage` was replaced by its shortcut link. It now removes only its own unfinished update download and replaces only its own link.
- **A failed update check says what really happened, not "offline?".** A busy or failing update server (an HTTP error such as 503, or a rate limit) and an error inside the app were all reported as "can't be reached (offline?)" / "Are you online?". The app, firmware, Development channel and DualSense Proton checks now say which it was: the server didn't answer, it's limiting requests, it answered with an error (with its HTTP status), the feed failed its security check, or the check failed inside the app; in all 7 languages.
- **A firmware update cut short can't leave a half-written firmware that starts and hangs.** The update wrote the firmware's first sector (where the board looks for the firmware to start) first, so a write stopped partway (a pulled cable, a USB reset) could leave a board that tried to start the half-written image instead of waiting in BOOTSEL mode. The app now clears that sector before anything else and writes it last: until the very end there is nothing to start, so the board comes back in BOOTSEL mode by itself and the app offers to install again. The failure message no longer says that unplugging and replugging recovers the board: if it doesn't show up, hold its BOOTSEL button while plugging it in and run the update again. When the firmware was fully written and only the restart failed, the app now says that instead of "no firmware running"; in all 7 languages.
- **Firmware updates are offered only to the board they are built for.** The app offered the newest published firmware to any connected board, so a Pico W was offered the Pico 2 W firmware (and then told to hold BOOTSEL, which could never work). Now an update is offered only when the feed has an image built for that board (board type, chip, flash size and controller persona), and any other board is told so instead (on a Pico W: "No firmware update is published for the Pico W yet."); today's feeds keep offering their firmware to the Pico 2 W. Firmware Back to stable now offers only the newest stable release, like the app's; while the stable feed's firmware isn't it yet, the app says so instead of showing "Up to date". In all 7 languages.
- **Firmware is written only to the board it is built for.** The first-time setup screen installed the Pico 2 W firmware on any board in BOOTSEL mode with an RP2350 chip, whatever the board. Now, before anything is erased (setup's Install, an update, Install again), the app reads the board in BOOTSEL mode: its chip (RP2040 or RP2350) and package (RP2350A or RP2350B, read the way Raspberry Pi's picotool does, including its workaround for A2 chips) and, when the flash isn't blank, its flash size. Another chip, or less flash than the firmware needs, is refused with the reason, and nothing is written ("This board has an RP2350B chip, and this firmware is for the Pico 2 W (RP2350A). Nothing was written."). A blank Pico whose flash size can't be read is never written silently: the setup screen asks first (Install / Cancel; Cancel writes nothing). A Pico 2 (no wireless chip) can't be told from a Pico 2 W in BOOTSEL mode, and the Pico 2 W firmware never starts on it: after the firmware didn't start three times on the same board, the setup screen stops offering it and says why. In all 7 languages. The readings are checked against a real Pico 2 W before release.
- **A board that stops answering isn't shown as live any more.** A request to the board had no time limit and the once-a-second check ignored its failures, so a board that stopped answering (still plugged in) kept showing its last state as current while every later request waited for ever. A request now gives up after 3 seconds with a plain message, and after three missed checks in a row the app says the board isn't answering and what you see may be out of date (unplug it and plug it back in); the notice goes as soon as it answers again. In all 7 languages. While the window is hidden in the tray, the app now reads only the board's status, not all its settings.
- **Games: Undo can be tried again after it failed partway.** When Undo couldn't put back one file (a launcher held it), the files it had already put back then read as "changed since the backup", so the change could never be undone. Files already back to their original are now skipped.
- **Linux: the version before an update stays, and the menu entry can't end up pointing at nothing.** At start the app deleted every older AppImage of itself beside the running one; it now keeps the newest older one, so you can go back to it. The link the menu entry and autostart use is now replaced in one step.
- **GNOME without tray icons: closing the window quits instead of hiding the app for good.** On GNOME without an AppIndicator extension there are no tray icons, so Close to tray (on by default) hid the window with no way back. The app now notices that: closing quits, it doesn't start minimized, and App settings → Startup says so in place of those two switches. In all 7 languages.
- **The last English error texts are in your language:** a press on the board's screen or keys the board didn't take, a picture the system couldn't read for the clipboard, an empty GIF recording, an incomplete button layout and an inconsistent game-file change. In all 7 languages.
- **A game rated before a fix says "before version X of this app"**, not "before DS5 Dongle X". In all 7 languages.
- **Windows' USB repair says why it has no Undo:** Windows creates the device entries it removes again by itself the next time the board (or a DualSense on USB) is plugged in. In all 7 languages.
- **A damaged firmware file can't ask for a write outside the flash.** The app now refuses a file whose blocks are bigger than the format allows, or lie outside the flash of the board the firmware is for, before anything is written.
- **Screen readers can jump from section to section:** every section header in the side panel is now a heading. Nothing changes on screen.
- **Diagnostics → Timing marks the speaker stage late from 10.67 ms**, one audio frame's real time (512 samples at 48 kHz), not from 10 ms.
- **A second launch in the first moments after start no longer makes a window before the app is ready.**
- **Auto Haptics' Fallback hint gives the real wait: about 0.1 s, not about 1 s.** The firmware lets derived haptic feedback in after the game has sent no haptic feedback for about 0.1 s; the hint said about 1 s. In all 7 languages.
- **Development builds on macOS: Developer → Fake games no longer shows.** It had nothing to fill there (the Games page runs on Linux and Windows), so the switch did nothing.

### Security

- **The installed app can't be used as a general Node.js runtime, and its app.asar is checked.** The app is now packaged with Electron's fuses set: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` and `NODE_OPTIONS` are ignored, the app loads only from its own app.asar, and on Windows and macOS that file is checked for changes at start. Redirects and frames can't take the window anywhere but the app's own page either.
- **Released builds turn off both debugger entry points.** A stable release now ignores `--inspect` (the main process's debugger) and quits at once when started with `--remote-debugging-port` or `--remote-debugging-pipe`, so no other program on the computer can attach a debugger to it that way. Development builds keep both for the test tools.
- **The update feed must be the channel's own and never older than one the app already checked.** A signed feed for another channel (Stable's builds served as Development's, or the other way round) or an older signed copy served again was accepted, and Back to stable installed whatever version the stable feed named. The app now refuses such a feed and says why (not "offline"), remembers the newest feed date it checked per channel (compared feed to feed, never against the computer's clock), and Back to stable installs only the newest stable release; in all 7 languages. Today's feeds keep working until they are republished in the new format.
- **Stable releases ignore the developer's local test update feed.** The loopback test feed (`DS5_UPDATE_MANIFEST`, with its test key) now works only in development builds; a stable release always asks GitHub for updates, whatever its environment says.
- **Electron 45.2.1 (stable), up from the 45 beta.** Fixes CVE-2026-115570: Electron did not block the compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, so connections signed by them were trusted. Chromium 156.0.8078.75, Node 24.22.1.
